correctness.rationale: A finite-graph energy argument proves eventual period at most two. Fixed- or two-periodic states with a nonflipping hub reduce to a single unanimous fixed state for each hub bit via the connected two-walk relation of a path with endpoint loops. Every hub-flipping two-cycle corresponds bijectively to an auxiliary-cycle word with no isolated ones, more than half of its vertices one and fewer than half of its edges one-one. The cyclic run-composition formula counts these exactly. The wheel comparison follows from one or two step-two cycles according to the parity of the rim. Direct exhaustive fan and wheel orbit simulations agree across all tested sizes, independently of the proof.

The graph-specific AND/OR auxiliary-cycle reduction gives a new direct classification and the exact even-size sign reversal. The wheel comparator is treated directly and does not imply the fan-edge-deletion assertion. This is a best-knowledge originality assessment, not a proof of global uniqueness.

value.rationale: Removing precisely one rim edge from a wheel is a natural minimal perturbation. The theorem resolves all recurrent orbit counts on the full fan family, identifies an exact odd-size invariant despite the graph change, and proves contrasting even-size outcomes where an edge deletion suppresses or creates oscillations. This is structural recurrence information, not a gratuitous finite slice or mere raw enumeration.
